## F-R42-01 — Codex daemon queue has no enforced disposition

Plan locations: Locked decisions lines 31-34 (D1/D5/D6/D7); host binding table lines 85 and 89; P0.2 line 174; P0.8 line 180; A9 line 595; Phase A live check line 637. Corresponding FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC005 and FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-008 capability rules are affected.

Defect: P0.2 run 2 uses `codex --no-daemon` and explicitly does not probe `codex queue`. It directs P0.8 to list queue messages as outside verified arrival paths. A9 then installs `UserPromptSubmit` hooks for Codex generally, and the Phase A live assertion tests `codex exec`. The plan gives no daemon-session guard, no queue-origin refusal, and no daemon-queue arrival test. A queued message can therefore reach the globally enabled hook with unknown timing or `turn_id` identity and still be minted or written as if the host were supported. The plan cannot establish D5 or D6 for that route. This is material because one user request may be minted when processed or conflated with a running turn, and the gate has no test to catch it.

Evidence: local `codex queue --help` says `Queue a message for an existing session` with `--thread` and `--message`; local `codex --help` says `--no-daemon` runs without the shared background server. Plan line 174 states the queue command reaches only daemon-hosted sessions and is unprobed. The current Codex plugin has no `hooks/hooks.json` before A9. No queue-specific Codex runtime case appears in A9 or the Phase A live check. The operator's D5/D6 text in plan lines 32-33 requires enqueue minting or `turn_logging_unsupported`, and line 85 requires the P0.2 per-host finding.

Fix to PASS: extend P0.2 with an observer probe in a daemon-hosted Codex session that receives `codex queue` during a running tool call, verifying UserPromptSubmit time against enqueue and a distinct stable `turn_id`. If it passes, add recorded payload fixtures and RED tests in A3/A9 plus a live rollout assertion. If it fails or cannot be observed, specify a runtime guard that refuses session-log verbs with `turn_logging_unsupported` for the affected daemon route (or all daemon-hosted sessions when queue origin is indistinguishable), with zero-mint/zero-write tests. Propagate the disposition to FR/TR/TEST ACs, the feature matrix, the 30-task TODO metadata, and the handoff. D6/D7 already authorize the unsupported branch. Classification: implementer plan edit; operatorDecisionFails: none.
